summary: Reconcile a repaired catalog rebuild's Core receipt with its Controller-visible command outcome. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The catalog-rebuild guide already directs an exact-ID retry after repairing a pending scan failure; operator steps do not change.

api.reason: The existing Core operation and managed-outcome APIs now agree after an exact catalog retry; routes, schemas, authentication and authorization are unchanged.

roadmap.reason: Closes a recovery defect in the current destination acceptance matrix.

state.reason: Core owns the existing metadata receipt, managed-command journal and catalog. A fresh Controller adopts the matching terminal outcome through authenticated Core inventory.
state.record: Existing pool-master backup metadata receipt, managed-command journal entry and catalog index.
state.adoption: Authenticated Core managed outcomes, backup operation result and catalog inventory.

verification.method: A focused regression failed with a stale attention journal before the fix and passed with terminal receipt/journal convergence afterward. Forced receipt-write failures reproduced masked errors before correction; focused success/failure and crash-gap tests now pass. Independent review found persistence propagation and authority-admission classification gaps; a red/green admission test confirmed that replica-capacity refusal remains retryable while actual receipt writes are fatal. On a matched fixed-build disposable NFS fixture, the preserved old operation converged on startup. A fresh one-byte-corrupt point was refused without VM or pin; after byte-exact repair, the same Core rebuild ID settled the receipt, journal and live Controller task, imported one point and preserved old hashes and a protected two-disk restore. Full local Go, Python, web, API, documentation, privacy and diff checks passed before that native retest.
verification.limits: The native result covers one disposable NFS profile and planted two-disk markers. SMB3/S3 corrupt-rebuild checks, later candidate changes and forge CI remain open.
